verdict_reasoning.description: The adversarial verifier's own words for why it returned `verdict`, copied from artifact.verify's `reasoning` when that verdict was applied. artifact.verify.json has always described this text as journaled verbatim so that 'why is H-012 refuted' is answerable three days later, and nothing kept it: the artifact_applied journal record carries the verdict's effects, not its content, and the only surviving copy was the artifact file in inbox/applied/, which the report renderer cannot read. Appendix A prints it -- a reader auditing a claim needs the argument, not a score. OPTIONAL, and absent means 'no verdict has landed yet, or this node predates the field'. Not required, because this schema is additionalProperties: false and adding a required field retroactively invalidates every hypothesis already on disk: each drops out of Graph.readable, rescores to 0 and has its facts quarantined on the first submit after the upgrade, irreversibly, since promotion only happens when a fresh verify verdict lands. See citation.json's page_sha256 for that same mistake costed out in full, and assumption.json's `cascaded` for the same absent-means-default convention.
